T: Paul Sheldon used to write for a living. Now he's writing to stay alive.
D: A famous novelist crashes in a Colorado blizzard and wakes up in the farmhouse of his number one fan, who will not let him leave.
P: Pour the champagne when Paul finishes the book and sends Annie for a glass.
S: Cream of tomato soup with cheese toasts
Cream of tomato soup with cheese toasts. Before the soup gets spilt.

Soften the onion and garlic in the butter. Add the tomatoes, stock and sugar and simmer for 15 minutes. Blend until smooth, stir in the cream and season. Pile the cheddar on the baguette slices and grill until bubbling, then float them on the soup.
Crisp paprika barbecue wings. Dirty birdy wings.

Pat the wings dry and toss with the baking powder, paprika, garlic powder and salt. Bake on a rack at 220C, turning once, until crisp. Toss with the warmed barbecue sauce and honey. Mix the sour cream, mayo, chives and garlic into a ranch dip and serve.
M: Paul's pills go into Annie's wine

Soak the breadcrumbs in 60ml milk, then mix with the beef, onion, garlic, egg, thyme and salt and shape into a loaf in a lined tin. Stir the tomato sauce, sugar and vinegar and spread half over the loaf. Bake at 180C, glazing again halfway, until cooked through. Meanwhile boil and mash the potatoes with the butter and milk and steam the beans. Rest the loaf for 10 minutes, slice thickly and serve with the mash and beans.
Beef pot roast with carrots and potatoes. The sow is called Misery.

Season the beef and brown it well all over in the oil, then lift out. Soften the onions and garlic, stir in the tomato paste and flour, then the stock. Return the beef with the thyme and bay, cover and cook at 160C for 2 and a half hours. Add the carrots and potatoes and cook until everything is tender. Slice or pull the beef and serve with the vegetables and gravy.
W: Chocolate self-saucing pudding. The penguin always faces due south.

Whisk the flour, caster sugar and 30g cocoa, then whisk in the milk, butter, egg and vanilla and spread in a buttered dish. Mix the brown sugar with the rest of the cocoa and scatter it over the batter. Pour the boiling water gently over the back of a spoon. Bake at 180C until the top is firm and the sauce bubbles underneath. Rest 5 minutes and serve with ice cream.
30g cocoa powder, plus 2 tbsp for the topping@Pantry
K: Chilled Champagne with a twist of lemon. The ritual when a book is done.
Twist a strip of lemon peel over each chilled flute and drop it in. Pour the champagne slowly and serve straight away.
